clue.text: Military force, say, encapsulated by brave character

indicators.note: something encapsulated by another is enclosed within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the lion is the proverbial emblem of courage
say introduces an example, abbreviated as e.g.

explanation.surface: An army, so to speak, wrapped up in a courageous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit, and the word still names any large body of soldiers.

clue.text: Some slap son after effrontery, wanting credit

indicators.note: after puts the son piece behind the effrontery piece

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, effrontery
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A cheeky son, lacking money, gets a smack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap' is British slang for make-up, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is one kind of make-up, which British slang calls slap.

clue.text: Drop in allowance? It could show degree in fall

definitions.text: It could show degree in fall

indicators.note: in places the drop word inside the allowance word

parts.note: a grant is an allowance of money
to die is to drop, as in drop dead

explanation.surface: A cut in a grant might be measured by how steeply things fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient measures steepness, the degree by which a slope descends.

clue.text: In the past, twice giving casual look

parts.note: once means formerly, in the past
twice says the phrase in the past is used again, now as over, meaning done and gone

explanation.surface: Long ago, someone glanced idly two times.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves mean 'in the past': ONCE as formerly, OVER as finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a quick, superficial inspection or glance.

clue.text: Child's first out of bed to enter part of kitchen

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word Child

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
to board a ship or train is to enter it

explanation.surface: A toddler climbs out of bed and wanders into the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a storage unit fitted in a kitchen, one of its standard fixtures.

clue.text: Bar group's excited about food's introduction — it's readily available

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the food letter
excited means stirred up, so the letters of Bar group's are jumbled
introduction asks for the opening letter of food

explanation.surface: A pub crowd gets worked up when the snacks first arrive, all free to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up for grabs is available to anyone who wants it.

clue.text: Demand to jump into punt for hamper

indicators.note: to jump into puts the demand word inside the punt word

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a gamble
to ask is to demand

explanation.surface: An order to leap into a flat boat for a picnic hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests a river boat; it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large basket, often with a lid, used for picnics.

clue.text: Rising sign of approval is following a handsome figure

indicators.note: following puts the pieces after the letter a
rising in a down clue means read upwards, so the approval word is reversed

parts.note: a nod signals approval
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rising nod comes after a good-looking man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth, so his name now means any handsome man.

clue.text: Show hesitation as one working in trench — cold must be ignored

indicators.note: must be ignored says the letter for cold is dropped from the trench worker

parts.note: a ditcher digs and maintains ditches
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A digger in a cold trench wavers but must press on.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be indecisive, wavering instead of acting.

clue.text: Location announced for swimmer

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for location is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a location is a place

explanation.surface: A venue is revealed for a swimming competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person in a pool, but here it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Where unprofessional film actor might go for a peripheral part?

definitions.text: Where unprofessional film actor might go
definitions.meaning: an actor who behaves badly may walk off the shoot, the filming session
a side branch growing out from the main stem or body

explanation.surface: A badly behaved film actor storms off, but ends up with a minor role.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side shoot from a plant, or any branch growing off a main body.

clue.text: Support for snaps shown by retired party after excursion

indicators.note: after places the party piece behind the excursion piece

parts.note: an excursion is a trip

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A camera stand comes out at a party held after a day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand that holds a camera steady for photographs.

clue.text: Perhaps service policy reveals limit in growth

parts.note: the service tree is a kind of tree, so service is an example of one
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A service's policy shows a cap on expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a business or army term; it is the service tree, a relative of the rowan.
explanation.definitionFit: The treeline is the altitude or latitude beyond which trees stop growing.

clue.text: Decline in male race

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
a race or people is a nation

explanation.surface: A downturn among the men in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a loss of activity or growth, a falling off.

clue.text: Guess Conservative starts to justify economy's course? True for a change

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the next three words
for a change says the letters of the word True are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory speculates on how to justify the economy's direction, insisting a change is right.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjecture is an opinion formed without proof, a guess.

clue.text: Flower left in a climate unusually with no end of heat

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the rearranged letters
unusually says the remaining letters appear in an odd order
with no says a letter is taken away from a climate
end of asks for the final letter of heat

explanation.surface: A bloom survives in a strange climate without any heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T from A CLIMATE leaves ACLIMAE, which is rearranged around L.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is a flowering shrub with glossy leaves and rose-like blooms.

clue.text: Endlessly go round motorway before quiet minor engagement

indicators.note: before puts the motorway piece ahead of the quiet piece
endlessly means without its last letter, so the word for go round loses its end

parts.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Drivers circle the motorway endlessly before a small, quiet wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway, its 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a brief, small-scale fight, a minor military engagement.

clue.text: Part of ground revealed something exceptional

parts.note: a stand is a seating section of a sports ground
a secret that is out has been revealed

explanation.surface: A section of a stadium showed off something special.
explanation.definitionFit: A standout is someone or something conspicuously better than the rest.

clue.text: A request given backing with noise in a set of peers?

indicators.note: given backing means turned backwards, so the word for request is reversed

parts.note: to beg is to request
a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A plea, supported amid din, among a group of nobles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' suggests lords; here they are people of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: An age bracket is a group of people of similar age, that is, contemporaries.

clue.text: Collection including very loud rubbish

indicators.note: including means the collection word holds the loudness letters inside it

parts.note: a pile is a collection or heap
ff is the musical notation fortissimo, very loud

explanation.surface: A heap of junk, with something blaring among it.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is nonsense, talk that is so much rubbish.

clue.text: Re-evaluate as everyone at heart becomes relaxed

indicators.note: at heart says the letters sit inside the words before it, across their joins

explanation.surface: A rethink, shared by all at its core, calms everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease means free from worry or awkwardness, comfortable.

clue.text: Camper ditching load on English river, causing grave difficulty

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away, so letters are taken out of Camper

parts.note: an electrical load is measured in amps
the Isis is the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A camper dumps their pack by an English river, which leads to serious trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty.

clue.text: Part of winter valued for a break

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the winter is prized as time off.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause, such as the break between acts of a play.

clue.text: Urn one's broken in cell

indicators.note: broken says the letters of Urn one are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An urn has been smashed in a prison room.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, a basic unit of the nervous system.

clue.text: Leading project? Female falls behind with it

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A trendy woman trails behind on the main scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagship project is an organisation's leading, most prominent one.

clue.text: Work online revealing meteorological phenomenon

indicators.note: work as a verb here means to knead or reshape, so the letters of online are reworked

explanation.surface: Remote working uncovers a weather event.
explanation.definitionFit: El Nino is a periodic warming of the Pacific that disrupts weather worldwide.

clue.text: Anglican event nonetheless no good

parts.note: even so means nonetheless

explanation.surface: A Church of England occasion is, all the same, a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening service of prayer, sung in cathedrals and churches.

clue.text: A companion divides prepared bag of medicine?

indicators.note: a piece that divides another splits it apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: set means prepared, as in ready, steady
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend splits up a ready-made bag of pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed packet, often holding a dose of powdered medicine; the question mark flags that as one example.
